rationale: Executor failed a discovery / identify-all task (find every payment record in a confirmed fraud incident) with 0% score: submitted 201 records as fraud, of which only 8 of 18 actual fraud records were correct (193 false positives). The grader rejected with 'answer contains too many invalid references'. The Executor ran 5 anomaly signal families (shared PMF across customers, shared device across customers, observed-location >50km from store, amount vs payment_lines mismatch, multiple payments per basket). Four returned 0 matches; only the geographic threshold returned 201 records — and the Executor submitted that lone signal's full output as the cohort. The geo threshold was 'validated' against a 5-record peek of unflagged records ('non-fraud sample: 0km, 0km, 0.1km, 14km, 16km — threshold clearly correct'), which cannot rule out a 10-20% FPR. The actual signal is a behavioural norm: customers buying online or picking up at a non-nearest store routinely sit >50km from the store they transact with. The current v0005 Discovery / identify-all section enforces recall discipline (rules 1-5: complete-set union of signal families, every pair member, two-signal-minimum coverage check) but has no precision discipline — it is consistent with the Executor's behaviour. v0004's own rollback note predicted exactly this opposite failure ('grader flags answers that include genuine records alongside fraudulent ones because the executor refused to narrow'). Fix: add rules 6-9 to the Discovery section (precision calibration for incident-shaped framing; threshold validation via bimodal-gap or 20-30 record sample, not 5-record anecdote; connectivity check using shared identifiers from sqlite_schema.txt to drop singletons; mandatory second-signal intersection for any single signal flagging >5% of scope) plus three matching anti-patterns. Also rewrites the OUTCOME_OK discipline paragraph and the Discovery preamble to name both failure modes symmetrically (low recall and low precision) so future Executors do not read the section as a one-way exhortation to broaden. No deletions of existing rules 1-5; rules 6-9 explicitly cross-reference rule 1 to prevent a future Executor reading them as permission to stop early.

rollback.strategy: Create a new version from v0005 content if rules 6-9 cause future Executors to under-submit on discovery tasks (e.g. drops legitimate cohort members because they happen to be singletons in the connectivity graph or because the only signal that catches them is a high-volume one); the safest narrower revert is to delete rules 6-9 and the three new anti-patterns while keeping the OUTCOME_OK discipline rewording and the Discovery-section preamble that names both failure modes symmetrically.
